CHAPTER  XL 

OF  HIS  PERFECT  PURITY  OF  CONSCIENCE. 

From  all  that  has  been  hitherto  related  of  the 
life  of  Blessed  Nicholas,  every .  one  will  easily 
understand  that  his  purity  of  conscience  must 
have  been  remarkable.  It  seems  certain  that  he 
preserved  his  baptismal  innocence  till  death ;  in- 
deed, this  is  affirmed  by  all  his  confessors,  not- 
withstanding his  declaring  himself  a  great  sinner; 
he  wept  over  the  little  failings  into  which  he  was 
occasionally  betrayed,  as  if  they  were  enormous 
sins.  It  was  sufficient  for  any  one  to  tell  him  that 
such  a  word  or  act  of  his  was  not  commendable, 
for  him  immediately  to  believe  himself  guilty  of 
a  great  fault,  and  to  have  recourse  to  confession. 
He  confessed  every  morning  before  he  celebrated 
holy  mass  ;  and  often  after  confession  he  would  re- 
turn two  or  three  times  to  accuse  himself  of  some 
slight  matter,  in  which  there  was  no  sin  at  all. 
This  frequent  return  to  his  confessor  before  he 
said  mass,  was  not  occasioned  by  scruples  or  vain 
apprehensions,  but  by  his  extreme  purity  of  con- 
science, which  made  him  look  upon  as  evils  those 
actions  which  were  simply  less  virtuous  and  less 
perfect.

Although  he  was  exceedingly  affable  and  edify- 
ing in  his  conversation,  he  kept  himself  as  retired 
as  he  could,  from  a  fear  of  falling  into  any  defect 
All  the  religious  who  lived  with  him  for  many 
years,  and  they  were  not  few  in  number,  bore 
witness  to  the  fact,  that  they  had  never  seen 
in  him  anything  amounting  to  a  venial  sin; 
this  testimony  is  striking,  considering  the  num- 
ber and  quality  of  the  witnesses ;  they  were  per- 
sons who  could  constantly  observe  his  conduct ; 
they  were  all  well  versed  in  theological  learning, 
and  well  skilled  in  the  exercises  of  Christian  per- 
fection. One  of  them,  a  very  learned  and  excel- 
lent religious,  who  was  his  confessor  for  four 
years,  hearing  his  confession  daily,  sometimes 
more  than  once,  declared  on  oath  in  the  processes, 
that  during  those  four  years  he  had  never  known 
Blessed  Nicholas  accuse  himself  of  anything  which 
he  could  safely  pronounce  to  be  a  venial  sin ; 
therefore,  to  give  him  sacramental  absolution, 
he  was  obliged  to  make  him  accuse  himself  of 
some  past  venial  sin.  Nevertheless,  in  all  his 
confessions  he  looked  upon  himself  as  being  the 
greatest  sinner  in  the  world  ;  he  struck  his 
breast,  and  wept  from  deep  and  intense  contrition. 
Sometimes  when  he  was  going  to  visit  his  great 
friend  S.  Lewis  Bertrand,  he  would  go  to  confes-

Brother  Nicholas,  blind  as  he  was,  saw  his  own 
heart  so  steeped  in  filth,  how  much  more  filthy 
and  abominable  would  it  appear  to  S.  Lewis  Ber- 
trand; therefore,  not  to  be  exposed  to  such

the  gift  of  the  continual  presence  of  God,  that

NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


he  always  thought  of  God,  and  always  loved 
God ;  hence  he  was  raised  to  the  highest  degree 
of  contemplation.  This  gift  of  sublime  prayer 
is  a  subject  beyond  the  reach  of  human  eloquence, 
and  largely  as  Blessed  Nicholas  was  endowed  with 
it,  he  knew  not  how  either  to  speak  or  to  write 
upon  it.  He  once  told  a  very  spiritual  friend  in 
confidence,  that  whilst  he  was  at  the  monastery 
of  the  Valle  di  Gesil,  he  once  wished  to  try  and  ex- 
plain the  meaning  of,  and  the  divine  effects  which 
he  experienced  in  contemplation  on  the  Supreme 
Good,  and  accordingly  took  up  his  pen  for  this 
purpose.  As  he  was  considering  the  subject,  with 
the  pen  in  his  hand,  he  heard  a  voice  from  heaven 
say  to  him,  "  Brother  Nicholas,  what  canst  thou 
say  of  me  ?  Dost  thou  conceive  thyself  able  to 
write  of  my  all  perfect  Being  ?  Be  silent,  com- 
pose thy  thoughts :  I  will  give  thee  my  grace." 
These  words  filled  him  with  indescribable  joy,  and 
he  fell  into  an  ecstasy,  which  lasted  a  considera- 
ble time.  If  Blessed  Nicholas  was  unable  to 
describe  his  elevated  prayer  and  contemplation, 
still  less  could  J,  or  any  one  else,  venture  to 
attempt  it.  I  will,  therefore,  merely  relate  a  few 
particulars  referring  to  his  assiduity  and  recollec- 
tion in  prayer,  and  of  the  efficacy  of  it,  particulars 
which  manifested  themselves  exteriorly,  and  which 
were  legally  attested  by  many. 

We  have  already  stated  that  every  night  after 
matins,  he  remained  praying  either  in  the  church 
or  choir  till  the  hour  of  prime.  On  the  great 
solemnities,  and  on  other  days  for  which  he  had  spe- 
cial devotion,  he  generally  spent  the  entire  night

from  complin  in  prayer ;  after  prime,  if  he  had 
not  to  confess,  or  to  exercise  some  ministry  of 
religion,  or  some  act  of  charity  to  the  poor,  he 
prepared  himself  for  mass,  celebrated,  made  his 
thanksgiving,  and  then  remained  in  prayer  till 
evening.  Every  morning  before  mass,  he  recited 
the  penitential  psalms,  with  the  litanies  and  pray- 
ers, and  always  recited  the  psalter  with  that  spirit 
of  fervour,  penetration,  and  divine  wisdom,  which 
guided  holy  David  in  the  composition  of  it. 

When  he  prayed,  either  in  his  cell  or  in  the 
church  at  night,  or  when  he  recited  the  office  with 
the  rest,  he  was  always  wholly  absorbed  in  God, 
and  generally  shed  tears  of  sweet  devotion.  Often 
in  the  day  did  he  remain  three  or  four  hours  on 
his  knees,  with  his  eyes  fixed  on  some  picture  or

his  Blessed  Mother,  or  with  S.  John  the  Evange-

weeping.  Over  and  over  again  did  he  use  these 
words,  "  My  God  and  my  all !"  and  for  hour  after 
hour  he  would  repeat  them  ;  his  fervour  sensibly 
increasing  at  each  repetition.  Whoever  happened 
to  see  him  in  prayer  was  struck  with  admiration 
at  his  recollection  and  devotion  ;  they  beamed  in 
his  countenance,  and  pervaded  his  whole  person ; 
his  sighs  and  tears  moved  the  spectators,  and 
filled  them  with  piety*  and  compunction.  A  reli- 
gious, a  fine  preacher,  fell  ill  in  the  monastery  of 
S.  Francis,  at  Valencia :  Nicholas  prayed  much 
for  him,  and  was  heard  to  say  with  most  fervent 
humility,  "  Lord  !  spare  this  Thy  servant,  who 
continually  brings  so  many  sinners  back  to  Thee  ;

and  lei;  me  die  instead  of  him,  for  I  am  utterly

Of  the  efficacy  of  his  prayers  with  God,  we  may 
judge  from  the  many  miracles  which  he  wrought  by 
them.  In  the  town  of  Xerica,  in  the  diocese  of 
Segorbe,  there  was  a  man  who  had  long  been  tor- 
mented by  the  devil  in  a  most  distressing  manner. 
He  made  a  confession  to  Blessed  Nicholas,  earnestly 
beseeching  him  to  pray  that  God  would  be  pleased 
to  deliver  him  from  this  heavy  trial.  Nicholas 
prayed  for  him,  signed  him  with  the  cross  on 
the  forehead,  and  told  him  that  from  thencefor- 
ward the  devil  would  molest  him  no  more ;  as  he 
said,  so  it  happened ;  and  from  that  time  till  his 
death  he  enjoyed  great  peace  in  his  various 
Christian  and  religious  duties. 

A  lay-brother,  a  good  simple  man,  belonging 
to  the  monastery  of  S.  Francis  at  Murviedro,  went 
one  evening  to  Blessed  Nicholas,  and  asked  him  to 
be  so  good  as  to  teach  him  how  to  pray  well.  The

holy  man  acceded,  and  told  him  the  different

"Let  us  go  down  to  the  church  together,  and

The  Passion  of  Jesus  Christ  was  the  usual  sub- 
ject of  his  meditations,  and  they  were  generally 
most  sublime  contemplations.  He  felt  an  ardent 
desire  to  feel  in  his  body  some  part  of  the  suf- 
ferings which  our  Lord  endured  for  us  whilst  He 
was  on  earth.  With  fervent  confidence  he  prayed 
for  this,  recommending  it  to  our  Blessed  Lady, 
and  to  the  beloved  disciple  S.  John.  Our  Lord 
granted  his  desire,  and  permitted  him  to  experi- 
ence the  most  excruciating  pain  all  over  his  body, 


Digitized  by 


508 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


so  that  he  was  sometimes  obliged  to  retire  into  a 
neighbouring  wood,  where,  with  a  load  voice  and 
groans,  he  would  recommend  himself  to  the  Mo- 
ther of  God,  to  S.  John,  to  S.  Mary  Magdalen, 
that  they  might  obtain  strength  for  him  to  bear 
up  under  sufferings  which  were  quite  above  the 
power  of  human  weakness.  Afterwards  he  was 
left  much  comforted  and  quite  joyful  in  conse- 
quence of  these  sufferings,  and  would  often  wander 
about  the  woods  and  hills,  like  a  man  out  of  him- 
self, weeping,  and  holding  long  colloquies  with 
Jesus  hanging  on  the  cross,  with  His  blessed 
Mother,  S.  John,  S.  Mary  Magdalen,  and  the 
other  holy  women  who  were  present  at  our  Lord's 
crucifixion,  acting  as  if  he  himself  were  on  Mount 
Calvary,  assisting  with  them  at  the  last  agony 
and  death  of  a  God  Man,  and  sharing  with  them 
in  the  passion  and  cruel  torments  of  their  common 
Lord.  And  here  again  he  became  inconsolable  at 
the  loss  of  so  many  men,  whose  obstinate  malice 
would  render  nugatory  the  infinite  merits  of  His 
Precious  Blood. 


CHAPTER  XIII. 

HIS  ECSTASIES. 

In  order  to  make  plain  to  all  the  inestimable 
gift  of  Blessed  Nicholas's  elevated  and  almost 
continual  contemplation,  God  would  glorify  him 
by  public  ecstasies.   Without  danger  of  exagge- 


Digitized  by  Google 


NICHOLAS  PATTORE. 


509 


ration,  I  think  I  may  safely  say  that  there  is 
scarcely  any  other  saint  of  whom  so  many  ecsta- 
sies are  related,  and  deposed  to  in  the  processes. 
For  many  years  he  fell  into  ecstasies  several  times 
a  day.  Alone  in  his  cell,  preaching  hefore 
numerous  audiences,  celebrating  holy  mass,  dis- 
tributing holy  communion  to  the  people,  in  public 
processions,  at  meals,  in  the  confessional,  in  the 
street,  in  all  places,  at  all  times,  he  was  liable  to 
them.  Many  of  these  ecstasies  have  been  already 
given,  others  are  now  to  be  given,  but  the  reader 
must  be  informed  that  those  specified  in  this 
compendium  are  but  few  in  comparison  with 
the  number  registered  in  the  processes ;  I  have 
taken  little  or  no  care  in  the  selection,  therefore, 
some  of  the  more  remarkable  may  have  been 
omitted.  From  information  which  I  have  ob- 
tained, and  from  the  processes,  I  gather,  that 
about  the  year  1550,  Blessed  Nicholas  being  then 
guardian  of  the  Valle  di  Gesu,  spent  the  whole 
of  Advent  with  extraordinary  fervour,  fasting 
more  rigorously  than,  usual,  and  practising  greater 
austerities,  by  way  of  preparation  for  the  approach- 
ing Christmas.  On  the  morning  of  the  23rd  of 
December,  as  he  was  celebrating  mass,  he  beheld 
just  after  the  consecration,  our  Divine  Lord  in  the 
form  of  a  most  beautiful  Infant,  who,  sweetly 
smiling,  said  to  him,  "  Brother  Nicholas,  wouldst* 
thou  very  much  like  to  see  Me,  and  adore  Me  as  I 
once  was,  in  the  crib  of  Bethlehem  ?"  This  sight, 
and  these  words,  made  Nicholas  feel  as  if  he  were 
already  in  Paradise,  and  of  course  he  answered 
yes.   He  then  saw  and  adored  the  Divine  Infant 


Digitized  by 


510 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


in  the  crib ;  from  this  mass  till  the  night  of  the 
Nativity,  he  revelled,  as  we  may  say,  in  the  joy  of 
the  Lord,  as  far  as  is  possible  in  this  mortal  life. 
But  on  the  solemnity  itself  his  bliss  vanished, 
and  he  found  himself  in  a  sad  state  of  painful 
aridity,  and  in  this  state  he  began  to  celebrate 
his  Christmas  masses.  On  coming  to  these  words 
in  the  first  Gospel :  "  And  she  brought  forth  her 
first-born,  and  laid  him  in  a  manger,"  a  lively 
image  of  the  vision  he  had  had  two  days  before 
arose  before  his  mind,  and  all  his  serenity  and  joy 
in  the  Lord  returned  ?  after  the  consecration,  he 
was  permitted  anew  sensibly  to  see  and  adore  the 
Infant  Jesus  in  His  crib,  whereupon  his  enjoyment 
was  at  its  height,  and  remained  with  him  the  whole 
morning.  At  grace  after  dinner  he  was  rapt  in 
ecstasy  in  presence  of  all  the  religious,  and  as  this 
was  the  first  time  they  had  ever  seen  him  thus 
carried  away,  they  were  utterly  astounded.  In 
the  monastery  of  S.  Francis  in  Valencia,  he  sung 
the  mass  of  Holy  Thursday,  and  had  to  give  com- 
munion to  the  religious,  and  to  several  other 
persons.  Scarcely  had  he  begun  to  give  com- 
munion, when  he  fixed  his  eyes  on  the  Blessed 
Sacrament,  and  became  immoveable  in  ecstasy. 
After  some  time  one  of  the  religious  took  the 
ciborium  out  of  his  left  hand,  but  could  in  no  way 
draw  the  consecrated  particle  from  between  his 
fingers,  and  finished  the  communions,  which  were 
very  numerous ;  not  till  then  did  the  holy  man 
return  to  himself ;  after  duly  depositing  the  con- 
secrated Host,  he  completed  the  solemn  offices ; 
the  excitement  of  the  people  who  witnessed  this 
spectacle  was  great,  but  quite  devotional.

Frequently  at  other  times  be  has  been  rapt  in 
ecstasy  whilst  distributing  the  holy  eucharistic 
bread,  when  it  was  sometimes  necessary  to  take 
the  ciborium  from  him,  and  finish  the  function, 
he  remaining  in  an  ecstasy  all  the  time.  Another 
time  when  he  was  giving  communion,  the  sacred 
particles  were  seen  to  move  and  pass  between  his 
fingers,  as  he  held  them  over  the  ciborium,  after 
the  manner  of  the  sparks  which  rise  from  a  red 
hot  piece  of  iron,  when  struck  on  an  anvil. 

In  a  procession  of  the  Blessed  Sacrament,  on 
arriving  at  the  public  square,  he  became  motion- 
less, with  his  lighted  taper  in  his  hand,  and  was 
seen  in  this  state  by  all  the  people  ;  the  procession 
advanced,  but  he  remained  immoveable  where  he 
was ;  several  persons  touched  him,  and  kissed  him 
with  great  respect  and  devotion,  though  he  was 
quite  insensible  to  all  that  passed  around  him. 
At  length  he  was  fairly  dragged  away,  to  prevent 
his  being  overpowered  by  the  crowd. 

A  courtier  belonging  to  the  viceroy  of  Valencia 
invited  him  to  dinner  ;  whilst  they  were  at  table, 
a  very  fine  painting  of  S.  John  the  Evangelist  was 
produced  and  admired;  scarcely  had  he  looked 
at  it,  than  taking  it  into  his  hand,  he  rose,  and 
begged  permission  to  retire  with  it  into  another 
room.  The  very  Rev.  Christopher  Moreno,  his 
companion,  suspecting  the  state  of  the  case,  went 
with  several  others  to  the  room  whither  the  holy 
man  had  retired ;  they  found  him  lying  on  his 
back,  with  his  hands  folded  across  his  breast,  his 
countenance  shining  like  a  seraph's,  his  eyes 
fixed  on  heaven,  he  was,  in  fact,  in  a  state  of 


Digitized  by 


512 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


exalted  ecstasy.  The  viceroy  was  informed,  who, 
together  with  several  of  the  nobles,  hastened  to 
witness  so  great  a  prodigy.  They  looked  at  him 
in  profound  astonishment,  and  many  of  them  shed 
tears  of  devotion,  blessing  and  thanking  the  Lord 
for  thus  favouring  and  glorifying  His  servant. 

Every  bird  that  he  heard  sing,  every  flower,  the 
fields,  the  hills,  heaven,  earth,  every  sort  of  crea- 
ture, reminded  him  so  forcibly  of  his  Creator,  as 
to  induce  ecstasies  many  times  every  day.  As  he 
was  once  travelling  through  an  agreeable  country, 
it  led  him  to  speak  of  God  to  his  companion,  bat 
he  almost  immediately  fell  into  an  ecstasy.  He 
spoke  of  Paradise,  and  of  the  Supreme  Good,  and 
running  to  his  companion,  he  embraced  him,  and 
raised  him  off  the  ground,  as  if  he  had  been  only  a 
feather ;  the  companion  feeling  convinced  that 
the  eloquence  and  energy  with  which  Nicholas 
then  spoke  and  acted  were  altogether  superhuman. 
On  returning  to  himself,  the  blessed  man  fell  at 
the  feet  of  his  companion,  with  deep  compunction 
accused  himself  of  being  an  enormous  sinner,  and 
then  kissed  his  feet. 

He  and  his  religious  brethren  of  the  monastery 
of  S.  Francis  at  Valencia,  were  making  the  pro- 
cession as  usual,  during  the  Octave  of  Corpus 
Christi,  when  on  returning  to  the  church,  Blessed 
Nicholas  was  rapt  in  ecstasy,  holding  his  lighted 
candle  in  his  hand,  which  was  taken  from  him, 
he  nevertheless  remaining  motionless  for  three 
hours  ;  he  then  extended  his  arms,  as  if  in  the 
act  of  affectionately  embracing  some  one  ;  he  next 
began  to  speak  of  God  in  most  tender  and  sublime

NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


513 


terms;  amongst  other  things,  he  said:  "And 
who,  0  Lord  !  can  it  have  been  that  said,  Brother 

Nicholas  will  Brother  Nicholas  be  good?" 

"Yes,  yes,"  after  some  space  of  time  he  replied  : 
"Yes,  yes,  Brother  Nicholas  will  be  good,  if  Thou 
wilt  make  him  good,  0  Lord ;"  and  he  continued 
talking  in  his  ecstasy  till  near  midnight. 

In  another  of  his  ecstasies  he  frequently  re- 
peated these  words:  "Say  to  the  just  man,  that 
it  is  well  in  the  end."  It  is  affirmed  that  he  dis- 
played such  exuberant  joy  in  this  ecstasy,  as  to 
show  that  the  repetition  of  these  words  was  most 
gratifying  to  him,  whence  it  was  conjectured  that 
the  former  ecstasy  had  revealed  to  him  the  fulness 
of  the  sanctifying  grace  with  which  he  was  en- 
riched,  and  the  second  his  infallible  predestina- 
tion. 

In  another  ecstasy  on  the  festival  of  the 
Assumption  of  our  Blessed  Lady,  he  uttered  these 
words ;  "  0,  great  Mother  of  God !  how  ineffable 
is  the  eternal  banquet  where  you  feast  at  the 
nuptial  *  supper  of  the  Immaculate  Lamb,  if  the 
little  drop  which  in  compassion  you  let  fall  into 
the  mouth  of  poor  Brother  Nicholas — and  he  is 
your  own  Brother  Nicholas — is  so  invigorating, 
that  he  would  willingly  allow  his  body  to  be 
chopped  into  a  hundred  pieces,  provided  his  soul 
could  but  spring  forth  and  mount  to  Paradise ! 

On  his  return  from  Madrid  to  Valencia,  some 
ladies  went  to  visit  him  at  the  convent  of  8. 
Maria  di  Gesfc ;  the  brother-porter  went  to  call 
him,  and  found  him  in  an  ecstasy  in  his  cell ;  he 
did  all  he  could  to  bring  him  to  himself,  but  to

no  purpose,  so  he  gave  up  the  attempt.  After 
Matins  in  the  night,  he  returned  to  Blessed 
Nicholas's  cell,  and  found  him  in  the  same  pos- 
ture, although  many  hours  had  intervened  since 
he  had  last  seen  him.  Out  of  devotion  he  em-

heard  of  none,  or  at  least  of  very  few  saints  in  the

may  be  added  that  his  fervent  ecstasies  in  no  way 
interfered  with  his  apostolic  or  religious  functions, 
in  the  exercise  of  which  his  whole  life  may  be 
said  to  have  been  spent. 


CHAPTER  XIV. 

HIS  CELESTIAL  VISIONS. 

To  the  gift  of  sublime  contemplation,  and  of 
almost  incessant  ecstasy,  our  Lord  likewise  added 
that  of  heavenly  visions,  with  which  he  was  pleased 
to  favour  Blessed  Nicholas. 

Whilst  he  was  in  the  monastery  of  S.  Maria  di 
Gesu  ,  Father  Baptist  Marcador,  an  old  man  of 
most  saintly  life,  passed  to  his  everlasting  home. 
As  usual,  the  corpse  was  carried  into  the  church ; 
on  passing  the  private  chapel  of  our  Lady  della 


Digitized  by  Google 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


515 


scala,  to  whom  Father  Marcador  had  been  greatlj 
devoted,  Blessed  Nicholas  would  have  the  body 
placed  within  the  chapel,  whilst  they  all  sang 
the  Salve  Regioa.  In  his  life-time,  the  deceased 
father  had  regularly  spent  a  considerable  time 
every  day  praying  in  this  chapel.  The  Salve 
being  ended,  the  holy  man  looked  at  the  image  of 
our  Blessed  Lady  with  great  joy  and  fervour, 
crying  out,  "Don't  you  see  him  ?  don't  you  see 
him  ?"  and  then  remained  in  an  ecstasy  for  some 
time.  On  returning  to  himself,  he  was  compelled 
by  the  religious  and  by  the  superior  to  tell  what 
he  had  seen.  With  humble  simplicity  he  said 
that  our  Lord  had  shown  him  the  soul  of  Father 
Marcador  environed  with  so  brilliant  a  light,  that 
the  sun  was  dull  and  cloudy  in  comparison 
to  it ;  that  he  saw  how  the  angels  conveyed 
the  holy  soul  of  that  worthy  religious  up  to  hea- 
ven, and  to  his  extreme  delight  he  had  beheld 
Jesus  and  Mary  welcome  him  into  the  eternal 
kingdom,  and  had  seen  the  immense  glory  and 
happiness  which  he  enjoyed. 

There  died  in  the  convent  of  the  Valle  di  Gesvl 
a  young  religious,  in  deacon's  orders,  named  Gon- 
salvo.  His  innocence  of  life  and  his  exact  regu- 
larity rendered  this  youth  specially  dear  to  Father 
Nicholas.  Our  Lord  showed  that  the  death  of 
this  young  brother  was  pleasing  in  His  sight,  by 
causing  the  corpse  to  exhale  a  most  extraordinary 
fragrance  whilst  it  was  exposed  in  the  church. 
Blessed  Nicholas  remained  as  usual  to  pray  in  the 
choir  after  Matins,  when  he  heard  a  melodious 
concert  of  Angels,  which  filled  his  soul  with  sweet 


Digitized  by 


516 


NICHOLAS  PATTORB, 


devotion,  and  at  the  same  time  oar  Lord  enabled 
him  to  see  that  those  angelic  choristers  were  ac- 
companying the  soul  of  Brother  Gonsalyo  to  hea- 
ven, where  his  saintly  life  was  recompensed  with  a 
brilliant  crown  of  glory. 

In  Valencia  there  died  a  certain  married  gentle- 
man of  exemplary  life,  merciful  to  the  poor,  exact 
in  frequenting  the  sacraments,  and  devoting  his 
whole  time  to  the  duties  of  his  state.  He  was 
much  beloved  by  Blessed  Nicholas,  who  assisted 
him  in  his  last  illness  and  at  his  death.  As  soon 
as  he  expired,  one  of  his  daughters  flung  herself 
in  a  state  of  inconsolable  grief  at  the  feet  of 
Blessed  Nicholas,  who,  with  great  cheerfulness, 
began  to  console  her,  saying,  "  Daughter,  be  com- 
forted, your  good  father  is  not  dead,  he  rests 
peacefully  in  the  sweet  sleep  of  the  Lord;  I 
beheld  the  inexpressible  delight  with  which  the 
holy  angels  waited  round  him,  and  welcomed  him 
into  heaven  ;  and  I  now  behold,  with  a  consolation 
which  I  cannot  describe  to  you,  his  present  union 
with  the  Sovereign  Good,  as  well  as  the  joy  with 
which  he  sings  the  infinite  mercies  of  God  towards 
him."  We  may  imagine  the  surprise  and  delight 
of  the  orphan  daughter  as  she  received  this 
assurance  of  her  good  father's  bliss ;  tears  rolled 
down  her  cheeks,  but  no  longer  were  they  tears 
of  grief,  on  the  contrary,  they  sprung  from  affec- 
tionate joy  and  holy  envy. 

When  Donna  Leonora,  Marchioness  of  Navarrei, 
heard  of  the  death  of  Donna  Joanna  of  Austria, 
the  foundress  of  the  royal  convent  of  discalced 
nuns  at  Madrid,  she  sent  for  Blessed  Nicholas  in

her  distress,  and  entreated  him  to  pray  that  the 
soul  of  this  great  princess  might  soon  be  admitted 
into  glory,  descanting  on  her  sanctity,  on  her 
religious  profession,  on  the  great  zeal  which  she 
had  manifested  for  the  faith  in  those  calamitous 
days,  and  on  her  favours  to  the  different  religious 
orders,  more  especially  that  of  S.  Francis.  The 
holy  man  answered  with  a  smile,  "  Lady,  the  soul 
of  this  most  pious  princess  is  already  in  the  enjoy-

meritorious  deeds."  In  astonishment  at  the

he  knew  this.  "  Ten  days  ago,"  replied  Nicholas, 
"I  was  celebrating  mass  for  the  soul  of  Donna

companied by  S.  Mary  Magdalene,  S.  Dorothy,  S.

her  glory,  and  of  the  gratitude  with  which  she 
will  for  eternity  bless  God  for  enabling  her  so 
heroically  to  despise  all  earthly  things,  to 
make  the  choice  of  holy  poverty  and  a  life  of 
penance."  Knowing  Blessed  Nicholas  to  be  so 
great  a  saint,  the  authority  of  his  words  completely 
satisfied  the  Marchioness,  especially  as  she  remem- 
bered that  Donna  Joanna  really  had  always  shown 
great  devotion  to  the  three  saints  mentioned  by 
the  holy  man. 

Whilst  he  was  guardian  at  Valle  di  Gesu,  he 
felt  a  strong  desire  to  behold  Jesus  Christ  in  the 
same  form  in  which  he  conversed  with  men  on 
earth.  He  begged  the  fulfilment  of  this  desire 
with  humble  confidence,  if  it  proceeded  from  the

518 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


Holy  Ghost ;  the  better  to  obtain  it,  he  prepared 
himself  with  prayer  and  extra  mortifications.  As 
he  was  one  day  imploring  this  favour  with  many 
tears,  our  Saviour  stood  before  him  ;  he  threw 
himself  at  His  adorable  feet,  weeping  more  fer- 
vently than  ever.  Jesus  spoke  to  him  with  great 
affection,  inebriating  his  soul  with  the  delight  of 
heaven,  and  said  to  him,  "  Brother  Nicholas,  be 
satisfied  now ;  your  desire  is  realized ;  from 
henceforth  I  will  always  remain  with  you,  unless 
you  voluntarily  leave  me." 

We  have  already  related  the  vision  with  which 
he  was  favoured  whilst  he  was  confessor  to  the 
nuns  in  the  convent  of  S.  Clare  at  Gandia ;  the 
reader  will  scarcely  have  forgotten  it.  Though 
in  effect  this  vision  seems  rather  to  have  been  a 
repetition  of  an  antecedent  vision,  in  which  our 
Blessed  Lady,  holding  her  divine  Son  in  her  arms, 
had  appeared  to  Blessed  Nicholas,  permitting  him 
to  hold  and  caress  the  Sweet  Babe,  he  at  the 
same  time  experiencing  and  evincing  a  strange 
alternation  of  joy  and  sorrow,  as  described  in  the 
first  book. 

On  a  festival  of  the  Epiphany  he  preached  in 
the  great  hospital  of  Valencia,  at  the  request  of  a 
pious  friend  of  his,  and  after  the  sermon  went  to 
diue  at  the  house  of  the  said  worthy  friend.  The 
whole  time  of  dinner  he  spoke  with  animated  fer- 
vour on  divine  subjects,  to  the  great  satisfaction 
of  the  guests.  His  own  meal  was  very  frugal. 
As  soon  as  dinner  was  over,  he  expressed  a  wish 
to  retire  to  another  room,  and  did  so ;  in  the 
mean  time,  several  persons  were  admitted  into

CHAPTER  XV. 

HIS  GIFT  OF  PROPHECY  AND  DISCERNMENT  OP 
SPIRITS. 

Not  only  did  Almighty  God  regale  our  saint 
frequently  with  heavenly  visions,  He  moreover 
often  permitted  him  to  penetrate  futurity,  and 
the  hidden  secrets  of  the  human  heart ;  a  faculty 
which,  as  every  one  knows,  can  come  but  from 
<3od  alone.

One  day  when  he  was  at  the  convent  of  S. 
Francis  in  Valencia,  having  merely  called  there 
as  he  was  travelling,  he  said  to  his  companion : 

Brother,  I  see  the  Turks  are  coming  upon  us 
in  great  fury,  and  in  hatred  of  the  Christian 
name."  His  companion  replied,  "Let  us  go  to 
the  church  to  implore  the  protection  of  the  Most 
High."  "  Go  to  confession  first,"  said  the  saint, 
41  and  then  we  will  both  go  and  pray  to  the  Lord." 
The  lay-brother  made  his  confession  to  the  saint, 
who  at  once  proposed  going  down  into  the  church, 
saying  that  a  great  battle  was  at  hand,  and  that 
the  Christians  stood  in  great  need  of  Divine  help. 
The  two  accordingly  went  into  the  church,  and 
before  beginning  their  prayer,  each  one  took  a 
severe  discipline.  Blessed  Nicholas  scourged  him- 
self so  unmercifully,  that  his  companion  thought 
him  going  to  excess,  the  floor  and  walls  being 
thickly  spotted  with  his  blood.  Suddenly  they 
heard  a  noise,  as  of  a  mighty  wind,  which  ex- 
tinguished all  the  church  lamps,  together  with 
a  riotous  confusion,  which  quite  bewildered  and 
stupified  them.  In  the  meantime  Blessed  Nicholas 
continued  scourging  himself  with  great  fervour ; 
however,  as  the  tremendous  noise  began  to  sub- 
side, so  did  he  begin  to  slaken  his  blows,  and  at 
length  exclaimed  with  a  cheerful  voice,  M  Victory ! 
victory ! "  In  a  short  time  the  noise  completely 
ceased,  and  a  profound  silence  reigned  through- 
out. With  a  sort  of  holy  fear  his  companion  pro- 
cured a  light,  and  on  looking  at  Blessed  Nicholas 
he  found  him  in  an  ecstasy,  and  with  a  very 
cheerful  countenance.    Finding  it  impossible  to

A  young  religious  went  to  him  one  morning,

Soon  after  this  the  young  man  determined  on

Donna  Joanna  of  Austria,  the  sister  of  king

John  di  Ribera,  one  of  the  royal  councillors  of 
Valencia,  fell  dangerously  ill,  to  the  great  regret 
of  the  public.  A  person  of  authority  asked  Ni-

rapt  in  an  ecstasy  and  remained  in  it  for  a  consider- 
able time.  The  person  who  had  made  the  request 
would  not  go  away,  being  anxious  to  know  the  re- 
sult, and  hoping,  too,  that  the  answer  would  be 
satisfactory.  The  ecstasy  being  over,  Nicholas 
said  to  him,  *'  Be  of  good  heart,  Sir,  and  tell  John 
from  me  that  he  will  not  die  of  this  illness."  'in 
a  few  days'  time  he  was  perfectly  well.  At  the 
end  of  a  year  and  a  half  Ribera  again  fell  ill,  and

A  citizen  of  Valencia  had  a  son  in  the  service 
of  his  Majesty,  and  engaged  with  his  regiment  in 
Flanders.  His  mother,  who  tenderly  loved  him,

went  to  Blessed  Nicholas,  beseeching  him  to  pray 
for  the  young  man's  safety  ;  he  always  answered, 
that  God  would  send  him  home  alive  and  well. 

Happening  one  day  to  call  at  the  mother's 
house,  he  found  her  unusually  anxious  and  fearful, 
because  she  had  been  a  long  time  without  receiv- 
ing any  tidings  of  her  son.  Nicholas  tried  to  con-

rest  assured  that  your  son  will  sail  from  Flanders 
on  the  Immaculate  Conception,  and  will  arrive  at 
your  house  alive  and  hearty  on  the  Epiphany." 
This  prediction  was  fulfilled  to  the  very  letter ;  the 
son,  however,  had  been  exposed  to  great  dangers 
during  the  voyage,  and  ascribed  his  escape  to  the 
prayers  of  Blessed  Nicholas.

ical  S.  Francis,  which  led  S.  Pascal  to  say,  that 
amongst  the  many  graces  with  which  God  favours 
His  chosen  servants,  is  that  of  revealing  to  them

the  number  of  your  own  sins  ;  in  this  your  hum-

tempt of  self,  with  a  holy  fear  of  God,  and  a  heartfelt 
sorrow  for  your  sins.  But  was  it  not  our  loving 
Lord  who  so  speedily  filled  your  intellect  with 
His  light,  and  enabled  you  clearly  to  discern  the 
state  of  your  soul,  showing  it  to  you  more  pure 
and  clear  than  crystal,  and  brighter  than  the  light 
of  the  stars  and  sun  P  Brother  Pascal,  you  then 
beheld  in  your  own  soul  the  most  exact  and  lively 
copy  of  the  divine  invisible  beauty,  which  raised 
and  blessedly  drew  you  into  a  high  contempla- 
tion of  the  Supreme  Good,  as  He  is  in  Himself. 
And  whilst  you  were  in  that  blissful  slumber,  what 
flames  of  divine  love  were  enkindled  in  your 
heart*  they  in  a  manner,  destroyed  your  nothing- 
ness, and  almost  changed  you  into  a  divine  being, 
making  you  enter  into  the  joy  of  the  Lord,  with  a 
fullness  of  content  and  happiness,  which,  though 
you  then  experinced  it,  neither  you,  nor  any  one 
else  on  earth,  would  ever  be  able  to  explain."

S.  Pascal  was  almost  beside  himself  with  astonish-

CHAPTER  XVI. 

MANY  OTHER   MIRACLES  WROUGHT   DURING   THE  LIFE- 
TIME OF  BLESSED  NICHOLAS. 

Amongst  the  miraculous  gifts,  styled  by  theolo- 
gians gratis  data,  there  is  one  called  the  grace  of 
restoring  health  under  circumstances  and  in  a  man- 
ner opposite  to,  or  superior  to,  the  ordinary  course 
of  the  laws  of  cause  and  effect.  And  as  these 
miraculous  cures  preserve  or  restore  health  or 
life  to  man,  which  are  the  first  of  his  temporal 
blessings,  these  miracles  are  therefore  very  much 
admired  and  applauded  by  the  generality  of  man- 
kind.  Almighty  God  favoured  Blessed  Nicholas 
with  this  gift  whilst  he  lived  on  earth,  in  proof 
of  which  I  will  insert  six  miracles  proposed  to  the 
Congregation  of  Kites,  when  it  was  judicially  ex- 
amining his  heroic  virtues,  and  the  divine  graces 
with  which  he  was  endowed;  omitting  many

532 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


others,  which  may  be  read  in  the  Processes,  and 
in  other  authentic  memoirs. 

Speranza  Monitor,  a  young  woman  of  Valencia* 
was  suffering  from  a  burning  fever,  which  entirely 
deprived  her  of  her  senses.  In  this  state  she  fell 
out  of  bed  and  dislocated  her  right  shoulder.  The 
nature  of  the  dislocation,  added  to  her  already 
dangerous  illness,  prevented  the  surgeons  from 
restoring  the  limb  to  its  natural  position,  and 
as  the  case  was  desperate,  they  entirely  gave  it 
up.  For  three  months  the  arm  hung  down,  as  if 
it  were  a  dead  member,  with  the  exception  that  it 
occasioned  her  excruciating  pain  ;  about  this  time 
Blessed  Nicholas  accidentally  entered  the  poor  cot- 
tage of  Speranza,  and  found  her  mother  assisting 
and  comforting  her  as  best  she  could,  though  she 
herself  was  seriously  ill,  He  first  encouraged  the 
mother,  preparing  her  for  death,  assuring  her  that 
her  end  was  near,  for  that  in  a  short  time  she 
would  quit  this  world  ;  as  in  effect  she  did.  He 
then  addressed  himself  to  the  daughter,  bidding 
her  trust  in  the  protection  of  our  Blessed  Lady 
and  S.  Vincent  Ferrer,  that  by  their  intercession 
she  might  speedily  be  cured  ;  he  thrice  made  the 
sign  of  the  cross  on  her  injured  arm,  and  then 
went  away.  In  the  evening,  having  occasion  to 
use  her  dislocated  arm  in  assisting  her  mother, 
she  found  to  her  astonishment  that  she  could 
move  it  freely,  the  arm  had  resumed  its  natural 
position,  and  was  perfectly  vigorous  and  healthy. 
The  surgeons  who  had  attended  her  declared  the 
cure  to  be  evidently  miraculous, 

Father  Martin  Esteve  had  a  tumour  in  his  leg,

which  soon  became  a  large  deep  wound,  corrupt-

years,  with  the  exception  of  now  and  then 
going  a  few  steps  on  crutches.  Just  before 
Blessed  Nicholas  died,  Father  Esteve,  at  the 
suggestion  of  some  friends,  requested  to  be  carried 
to  the  holy  man,  who,  having  made  the  sign  of  the 
cross  on  the  leg,  bade  him  make  a  novena  in  hon- 
our of  the  Immaculate  Conception  of  our  Blessed 
Lady;  assuring  him  that  the  Mother  of  God 
cwould  cure  him.  At  the  end  of  the  novena  he 
was  perfectly  cured ;  nor  did  he  during  the  rest 
of  his  life  ever  feel  the  slighest  inconvenience  in 
the  leg  that  was  cured. 

Donna  Maria  Catala,  daughter  of  the  Count  of 
Castellan,  who  died  a  Franciscan  nun,  when 
quite  a  child  fell  from  a  great  height  into  a  canal 
which  ran  through  the  garden  under  the  windows 
of  her  father's  palace.  An  expert  swimmer  im- 
mediately plunged  into  the  water  to  rescue  the 
drowning  child,  but  so  impetuous  was  the  current, 
that  he  could  not  overtake  her  till  she  had  been 
carried  away  about  a  hundred  paces  from  the  spot 
where  she  had  fallen  in,  and  when  drawn  out,  she 
was  considered  to  be  dead.  Her  mother  was  incon- 
solable, and  taking  up  the  corpse  of  her  beloved 
child,  she  carried  it  to  Blessed  Nicholas,  beseech- 


Digitized  by 


NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


ing  him  to  bless  it,  and  through  the  divine  power, 
to  restore  it  to  her  alive  and  well.  Moved  to 
compassion  at  the  state  of  the  child,  and  the  pro- 
found grief  of  the  mother,  he  signed  the  little 
corpse  with  the  cross,  blessed  it,  and  said  thrice, 
"My  little  angel,  my  little  angel,  it  is  all  no- 
thing!" he  restored  her  to  her  mother  alive  and 
blithe ;  the  countess  was  overpowered  with  de- 
light and  astonishment. 

In  a  village  not  far  from  Valencia,  Ursula 
Colom,  a  peasant's  daughter,  had  suffered  from 
a  terrible  fistula  for  three  or  four  years ;  the 
effluvia  from  it  was  so  intolerable  that  no  one 
could  remain  near  her  for  any  length  of  time. 
Her  parents  had  spent  much  money  in  hopes  of 
her  cure ;  and  had  consulted  the  best  physicians 
and  surgeons  of  Valencia.  Ursula  was  ten  years 
of  age,  and  had  often  said  that  Father  Nicholas 
Fattore  could  cure  her  by  a  miracle ;  her  father 
was  a  man  of  no  piety,  nor  would  he  pay  any 
attention  to  the  words  of  his  innocent  child.  It 
so  happened  that  as  Blessed  Nicholas  was  one 
day  returning  from  the  country  to  the  monastery 
of  S.  Maria  di  Gesft,  he  passed  the  cottage  of 
Baptist  Colom,  whilst  Ursula  and  several  of  her 
neighbours  were  standing  at  the  door.  She  was 
told  that  Father  Fattore  was  passing  along,  when, 
assisted  by  a  companion,  she  hobbled  up  to  him 
with  great  difficulty,  and  kissed  his  hand.  The 
holy  man  blessed  her,  and  inquired  about  her 
malady ;  at  that  moment  Baptist  also  advanced, 
kissed  his  hand,  and  described  the  incurable  na- 
ture of  his  daughter's  complaint.   Nicholas  asked

what  remedy  was  applied  to  the  fistula ;  the  father 
answered  that  it  was  a  plaster  prescribed  by  the 
surgeons.  "The  plaster  is  useless,"  said  the 
saint,  "  take  it  off  immediately ;  Ursula  is  already 
cured."  Having  said  this,  he  pursued  his  way. 
Baptist  returned  home  with  his  daughter,  and  told 
his  wife  what  Father  Fattore  had  said.  In  pre- 
sence of  their  neighbours  the  fistula  was  un- 
covered, but  no  plaster  was  to  be  found,  and  the 
wound  was  perfectly  healed,  a  scar  only  remain- 
ing, about  the  size  and  shape  of  an  eye.  Baptist, 
beside  himself  with  joy  at  so  evident  a  miracle, 
ran  after  Blessed  Nicholas,  threw  himself  at  his 
feet,  kissed  them  again  and  again,  and  covered 
them  with  tears  of  grateful  delight. 

Our  Saint  was  invited  to  preach  for  the  octave 
of  Corpus  Ghristi  at  Affages  in  the  territory  of 
Tarragona.  He  went  there,  and  in  the  middle  of 
his  sermon  he  fell  into  an  ecstasy  before  all  the 
people,  who  were  moved  to  devotion  by  the  sight  of 
him.  After  the  sermon  he  was  taken  to  the  house 
of  a  farmer  named  John  Comte,  who  presented  his 
son  to  him,  a  child  of  two  years  old,  who  for  some 
months  had  suffered  from  a  dangerous  rupture. 
No  sooner  did  the  child  look  at  Blessed  Nicholas, 
than  he  exultingly  ezclaimed,  "The  saint  is 
come!  the  saint  is  come!"  The  holy  man 
knelt  down  at  the  child's  feet,  affectionately 
kissed  them,  and  said,  "My  dear  little  angel,  it 
is  you  who  are  the  saint,  I  am  a  great  sinner," 
Then  he  blessed  him  with  the  sign  of  the  cross, 
and  the  rupture  entirely  disappeared. 

At  Villanova,  Frances  Espelta,  a  child  of  about

twelve  years  of  age,  was  afflicted  with  the  falling 
sickness,  which  often  threw  her  on  the  ground  as 
if  dead,  and  deprived  her  of  her  senses.  Blessed 
Nicholas  was  then  at  the  monastery  of  Escornal- 
bou,  and  the  fame  of  his  sanctity  and  miracles 
were  spread  far  and  wide.  Some  women  of  Vil- 
lanova  were  going  to  Escornalbou  to  consult  the 
saint,  and  Frances  begged  to  be  taken  with  them, 
but  they  refused,  because  she  was  poor  and  so 
very  ill-clad.  She  continued  so  urgent  in  her 
entreaties,  that  at  last  they  agreed  to  let  her 
accompany  them.  On  arriving  at  Escornalbou 
they  asked  for  Father  Fattore,  Frances  placed 
herself  behind  the  rest  from  a  sense  of  shame. 
Blessed  Nicholas  at  once  fixed  his  eyes  on  her, 
and  said,  "  Poor  Frances  came  here  sick,  and  will 
go  home  well."  The  child  was  astounded  at  his 
words,  for  she  had  never  seen  him,  nor  had  he 
ever  seen  her  before  ;  he  spoke  to  her  very  com- 
passionately, put  his  hand  upon  her  head,  blessed 
her  thrice  with  the  sign  of  the  cross,  and  sent 
her  home  quite  well  and  happy,  nor  did  she  ever 
after  experience  the  slightest  symptom  of  her  old 
complaint.  In  due  time  she  married,  and  thirty- 
five  or  thirty-six  years  after  the  occurrence  she 
attested  it  on  oath  in  the  process  for  the  canoni- 
zation of  her  benefactor. 

"  These  six  miracles  are  sufficient  to  prove  the 
wonderful  gift  which  Blessed  Nicholas  had  re- 
ceived  from  God,  of  restoring  health  to  the  sick ; 
moreover,  many  others  may  be  read  in  the  pro- 
cesses juridically  attested.,,  Thus  spoke  the  pro- 
curator of  the  cause  to  the  Congregation  of  Rites,

and  I  maj  here  repeat  the  same.  I  will  neverthe- 
less  add  three  others,  copied  from  the  processes, 
in  which,  besides  the  restoration  of  health,  there 
was  likewise  the  miraculous  apparition  of  Blessed 
Nicholas,  although  he  was  alive  at  the  time.  A 
worthy  priest  was  recovering  from  a  long  and 
dangerous  illness,  when  the  devil  assailed  him 
with  a  violent  temptation,  which  sadly  disturbed 
his  mind  for  some  hours,  and  which  even  affected 
his  debilitated  body ;  a  violent  fever  was  the  con- 
sequence, and  being  exceedingly  weak,  the  relapse 
was  considered  dangerous  and  fatal.  This  took 
place  in  the  middle  of  the  day,  and  at  night  he 
was  considerably  worse,  so  much  so  as  to  alarm 
the  doctors.  About  midnight,  to  the  surprise  of 
all  he  fell  asleep  ;  in  his  slumber  he  saw  Blessed 
Nicholas  enter  his  room,  with  S.  Giles  (to 
whom  the  priest  had  a  great  devotion)  S.  Vin- 
cent Ferrer  and  S.  Lewis  Bertrand.  Blessed 
Nicholas  took  him  by  the  hand,  and  awoke 
him,  saying  :  "  Fear  nothing,  our  Lord  has  been 
pleased  that  these  saints  should  come  with  me  to 
visit  you,  and  to  assure  you  that  you  will  not  die 
of  this  illness  ;  you  have,  however,  many  trials  to 
encounter,  but  trust  in  the  Lord,  and  be  faithful 
to  Him,  He  has  hitherto  always  sustained  and 
assisted  you,  and  He  will  continue  to  do  so:  He 
then  blessed  him  with  the  sign  of  the  cross,  the 
vision  disappeared,  and  the  priest  found  himself 
perfectly  cured.  Another  time,  about  mid-day, 
Nicholas  again  appeared  to  him  with  S.  Giles, 
and  gently  scolded  him  for  having  that  morning 
omitted  his  usual  meditation,  strongly  advising

him  to  exactitude  in  that  holy  exercise.  Soon 
afterwards  he  appeared  to  him  for  the  third  time 
with  S.  Giles,  and  warned  him  of  five  very  im-

A  Doctor  of  Laws  belonging  to  Valencia,  went 
to  Salamanca  on  some  important  suit,  and  whilst 
there  fell  dangerously  ill.  On  the  twentieth  day 
of  his  illness,  he  began  to  fear  that  his  death  was 
now  at  hand ;  whereupon .  he  prayed  his  angel* 
guardian  to  inspire  Blessed  Nicholas,  then  at 
Valencia,  with  the  thought  of  praying  for  his 
recovery.  Having  done  this,  he  saw  Blessed 
Nicholas  with  a  companion  enter  his  room.  He 
sat  down  at  his  side,  began  most  kindly  to  console 
him,  told  him  he  would  not  die  of  that  illness,  and 
that  our  Lord  would  soon  cure  him.  He  made 
the  sign  of  the  cross  on  his  mouth  and  breast, 
held  his  hand  for  a  little  time  on  his  head,  and 
then  disappeared.  The  invalid  found  himself 
most  composed  and  happy  in  mind,  and  perfectly 
healed  in  body.  On  his  return  to  Valencia,  he 
called  on  Blessed  Nicholas,  and  with  tears  of 
gratitude  thanked  him  for  the  miraculous  visit  he 
had  paid  him  at  Salamanca,  and  for  his  restored 
health  ;  the  holy  man  smiled,  and  only  said,  "Be 
silent,  Santarelli — God  is  good !"  '

A  goldsmith  of  Valencia  had  a  wound  of  long 
standing  in  his  leg,  which  in  spite  of  medical  + 
treatment,  became  gangrened ;  the  doctors  recom- 
mended immediate  amputation,  as  the  only  means 
of  preventing  the  infection  from  spreading  to  the 
rest  of  his  body,  and,  in  fact,  from  destroying  his 
life.  The  poor  man  was  horrified  at  the  idea  of 
such  an  operation,  and  entreated  the  surgeons  to 
defer  it,  at  least  for  a  day.  In  the  meantime  he 
sent  for  Father  Nicholas,  and  earnestly  recom- 
mended himself  to  his  prayers.  The  saint  con- 
soled him  with  great  charity,  and  bade  him 
recommend  himself  to  S.  Francis,  S.  Vincent 
Ferrer,  and  S.  Ursula,  and  told  him  that  these 
Saints  would  obtain  the  favour  of  God  for  him.  In 
the  morning  of  the  following  day,  shortly  before 
the  hour  appointed  by  the  surgeons  for  the  ampu- 
tation, he  fell  into  a  gentle  slumber,  during  which 
he  saw  Blessed  Nicholas  enter  his  room,  who 
approached  the  bed,  made  the  sign  of  the  cross 
twice  on  the  diseased  leg,  and  disappeared.  Thei 
man  awoke  refreshed,  and  found  his  leg  free  from 
pain.  The  surgeons  soon  arrived  to  perform  the 
operation,  unbandaged  the  leg,  and  to  their  utter 
amazement  found  it  perfectly  cured.  One  and 
all  cried  out  that  a  more  evident  miracle  could 
never  have  been  witnessed. 

And  here  I  may  conclude  my  task,  reminding 
my  readers,  that,  far  from  being  a  history  of  the 
Life  of  Blessed  Nicholas  Fattore,  this  is  but  a  suc- 
cinct compendium  of  his  acts,  sufficient,  however, 
to  give  the  public  an  idea  of  his  admirable  and 
amiable  sanctity.    In  arranging  my  narrative,  I

NICHOLAS  FATTORE. 


have  not  chosen  profane  historians  for  my  models, 
but  those  holy  Greek  and  Latin  fathers  who  wrote 
the  Lives  of  the  great  saints  of  their  days  ;  I  know 
and  acknowledge  that  I  neither  have  the  power  or 
sweetness  to  copy  that  unction  of  spirit  with  which 
they  wrote,  although  the  sanctity  of  Blessed  Nicho- 
las might  well  inspire  it.  In  the  same  manner  I  have 
been  but  a  poor  copyist  of  their  correct  lights  and 
holy  eloquences,  elegancies  with  which  their  writ- 
ings are  so  copiously  adorned.  I  could  have 
wished  to  have  arranged  my  subjects  in  better 
chronological  order,  but  it  was  impossible.  Re- 
peatedly did  the  Congregation  of  Rites  complain 
to  the  Postulators  of  the  Cause  of  the  deficiency 
of  dates,  even  with  regard  to  many  of  the  most 
wonderful  of  the  miracles.  This  complaint  was 
raised  two  centuries  ago.  To  remedy  it,  it  would 
be  necessary  for  me  to  examine  all  the  registers 
and  manuscripts  of  those  times,  in  the  archives  of 
the  provinces  in  which  Blessed  Nicholas  lived,  a 
task  far  beyond  my  occupations,  and  impossible, 
considering  the  short  space  of  time  allowed  me  for 
writing,  and  the  place  in  which  I  write. 

Besides,  I  know  for  certain  that  this  long  and 
laborious  task  has  already  been  accomplished,  as 
far  as  it  was  possible,  by  the  Postulator  of  the 
Cause  at  Rome,  who  gave  a  full  account,  elegantly 
written  in  Spanish,  of  this  hero  of  the  Minor-Ob- 
servantines  of  S.  Francis.
